definition: Git is a distributed version-control system. Every clone holds the project's history, not only the latest files. A commit records a snapshot of the tree, and later commits point at their parent commits, forming a graph.
details: The conceptual model is a snapshot plus metadata, not a list of line edits. Storage may compress that snapshot as a delta.
examples: A local clone with the full history of a repository
A commit that points at its parent and at a tree of files
